description: Snowflake Scripting LOOP LABELS. The label is declared by the TRAILING label - END LOOP my_loop, END FOR sum_loop, END WHILE w - and referenced by BREAK <label> / CONTINUE <label>, which propagate OUTWARD through nested loops. All live-verified. The proof that the labelled forms are real syntax is that a BREAK naming no trailing label fails SEMANTICALLY there (Label 'MY_LOOP' not found) rather than as a syntax error. The one spelling Snowflake does NOT have is the LEADING declaration my_loop:, which stops at the colon - so that form is refused here. A trailing label needs no reference at all, a labelled BREAK naming the OUTER loop stops both loops, and a bare BREAK stops only the innermost, which is the pair that shows the label is doing the work. Converted 1:1 from scripting/LoopLabelTest (now retired); the blocks are written on one line here, which the scripting parser reads identically.

steps.sql: BEGIN LET i INTEGER := 0; my_loop: LOOP i := i + 1; IF (i >= 5) THEN BREAK; END IF; END LOOP; RETURN i; END;
BEGIN LET i INTEGER := 0; LOOP i := i + 1; IF (i >= 5) THEN BREAK my_loop; END IF; END LOOP my_loop; RETURN i; END;
BEGIN LET total INTEGER := 0; FOR i IN 1 TO 6 DO IF (MOD(i, 2) = 1) THEN CONTINUE sum_loop; END IF; total := total + i; END FOR sum_loop; RETURN total; END;
BEGIN LET total INTEGER := 0; FOR i IN 1 TO 3 DO total := total + i; END FOR any_name; RETURN total; END;
BEGIN LET i INTEGER := 0; WHILE (i < 3) DO i := i + 1; END WHILE w_loop; RETURN i; END;
BEGIN LET outerCount INTEGER := 0; FOR i IN 1 TO 3 DO outerCount := outerCount + 1; FOR j IN 1 TO 3 DO BREAK outer_loop; END FOR; END FOR outer_loop; RETURN outerCount; END;
BEGIN LET outerCount INTEGER := 0; FOR i IN 1 TO 3 DO outerCount := outerCount + 1; LOOP BREAK; END LOOP; END FOR; RETURN outerCount; END;
